questions.question: Which of the following duties is mentioned as the 11th Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To cherish and preserve the rich national heritage of our culture
To provide opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years of age
To protect the integrity and unity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years of age**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th Fundamental Duty** in the Indian Constitution is **To provide opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years of age**.
 
• This duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in **2002**.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of education and the role of parents or guardians in ensuring that children receive education.
 
• This duty aligns with **Article 21A**, which makes education a fundamental right for children in this age group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They were added by the **42nd Amendment Act in 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties, but the **86th Amendment added the 11th duty**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation and society.

questions.question: The census operations of India had been carried out in ________ phases according to census 2011.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **census operations of India** had been carried out in **two phases** according to census 2011.
 
• The first phase is called the **House Listing and Housing Census**, which involves listing all houses and collecting data on housing conditions, household amenities, and assets.
 
• The second phase is the **Population Enumeration**, which involves collecting information about all persons residing in India on the reference date.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every **ten years** by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first synchronous census in India was held in **1881**.
 
• The Census is a **statutory exercise** conducted under the provisions of the **Census Act, 1948**.
 
• The data collected through the census is used for **policy-making, planning, and administration** by the government.
 
• The Census also provides valuable information for **demographic research** and analysis.
 
• India's Census is one of the most comprehensive and detailed data collection exercises in the world, covering the entire population of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate founded Agra city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lodi dynasty**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lodi dynasty** founded the city of Agra in 1504.
 
• Agra was established by Sultan **Sikandar Lodi**, who was the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate from 1489 to 1517.
 
• The city of Agra later became one of the most important cities during the Mughal era, especially under the reign of Emperor Akbar.
 
• Agra is renowned for its rich history, including the construction of the Taj Mahal by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Delhi Sultanate** was a Muslim kingdom based mostly in Delhi that stretched over large parts of the Indian subcontinent for 320 years (1206–1526).
 
• It consisted of five dynasties: the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, the Khalji dynasty, the Tughluq dynasty, the Sayyid dynasty, and the Lodi dynasty.
 
• The Lodi dynasty was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate before it was conquered by the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Lodi dynasty is known for its architectural contributions and the establishment of new cities, including Agra.

questions.question: The National Youth Day or the 'Yuwa Diwas' is celebrated on which day in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 January**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Youth Day** is celebrated on **January 12th** every year in India.
 
• This day marks the birth anniversary of **Swami Vivekananda**, a prominent Indian Hindu monk and philosopher.
 
• The Government of India declared January 12th as National Youth Day in **1984** and it has been celebrated annually since **1985**.
 
• The aim of the celebration is to inspire and motivate the youth of India to follow the ideals and philosophies of Swami Vivekananda.
 
• Various events such as **youth conventions, seminars, and cultural activities** are organized across the country to commemorate this day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Swami Vivekananda's teachings focus on the importance of **youth empowerment** and the role of youth in nation-building.
 
• He is best known for his speech at the **Parliament of the World's Religions** in Chicago in **1893**, where he introduced Hindu philosophy to the Western world.
 
• Swami Vivekananda's message emphasizes **strength, self-reliance, and service to humanity**.
 
• His birthday, January 12th, is also observed as **Yuva Diwas** in several educational institutions across India.

questions.question: Harisena, the author of Prayag Prashasti, was the court poet of which of the following Gupta emperors?

• It is an important source of historical information about the Gupta Empire and its administration.
 
• The Prayag Prashasti is inscribed on an Ashokan pillar in Allahabad (now Prayagraj).

• His reign marked significant territorial expansion and consolidation of the empire.
 
• The Gupta period saw the flourishing of classical Indian culture, including the development of Sanskrit literature and the performance of classical music and dance.

questions.question: Which option is NOT correct in case of appointment of a Governor?

• A Governor is **appointed by the President of India** for a term of **five years**.
 
• The Governor must be a **citizen of India**.
 
• The Governor should be at least **35 years old**.
 
• During his tenure, the Governor **cannot hold any office of profit**.
 
• The Governor's term can be **extended or cut short** by the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Governor's powers and functions are similar to those of the President of India, but at the state level.
 
• The Governor plays a crucial role in the **state's administration** and acts as a link between the central and state governments.
 
• The **Governor's role** includes summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the state legislative assembly, among other duties.
 
• The Governor can also **grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment** or suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the state extends.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts abolished the East India Company's monopoly of trade with China?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1833**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** abolished the East India Company's monopoly of trade with China.
 
• This act was one of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company.
 
• The act marked the beginning of the end of the commercial activities of the company, focusing more on administration.
 
• It also allowed the company to continue its territorial possessions in India but under strict regulation by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** is also notable for making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, consolidating the administration.
 
• The act also introduced a system of open competition for the selection of civil servants, although it was not implemented until the 1850s.
 
• It is considered a significant step towards the centralization of the administration in India.
 
• Other important provisions included the establishment of a law commission and the codification of laws.

questions.question: Which of the following bacteria grow in milk and convert it to curd?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Lactobacilus** are responsible for the **fermentation **process that converts **milk into curd**.
 
• These bacteria produce lactic acid as a byproduct of lactose fermentation, which lowers the pH of milk, causing it to coagulate and form curd.
 
• Common types of lactic acid bacteria involved in this process include **Lactobacillus bulgaricus** and **Streptococcus thermophilus**.
 
• The production of curd is a traditional method of preserving milk and enhancing its nutritional value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Curd is a rich source of **probiotics**, which are beneficial bacteria that aid in digestion and improve gut health.
 
• It also contains essential nutrients like **calcium, protein, and vitamins**, making it a valuable addition to the diet.
 
• In many cultures, curd is used in a variety of dishes and is a staple in traditional cuisine.
 
• The fermentation process not only enhances the flavor of milk but also extends its shelf life.

questions.question: When a non-minister proposes a bill, it is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Private Member's Bill**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Private Member's Bill** is a bill introduced by a member of parliament or a legislative assembly who is not a minister.
 
• This is in contrast to a **Government Bill**, which is introduced by a minister on behalf of the government.
 
• Private Member's Bills can cover a wide range of issues and allow legislators not in the executive branch to propose new laws or amendments to existing ones.
 
• Such bills are an important tool for raising issues of public interest and can sometimes lead to significant legislative changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Private Member's Bills** are typically discussed only on Fridays when the parliament is in session.
 
• While the success rate of Private Member's Bills is relatively low compared to Government Bills, they play a crucial role in parliamentary democracy.
 
• One of the notable Private Member's Bills that became law was the **Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994** in India.
 
• Private Member's Bills must go through the same stages of scrutiny and debate as Government Bills, including multiple readings and committee reviews.
 
• The introduction of Private Member's Bills encourages a more participatory legislative process and ensures diverse viewpoints are considered in lawmaking.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor conductor of electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distilled water**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distilled water** is a poor conductor of electricity.
 
• This is because distilled water is free from salts and minerals that can carry electric current.
 
• On the other hand, **tap water, pond water, and hand pump water** contain dissolved salts and minerals, making them better conductors of electricity.
 
• Conductivity in water is primarily due to the presence of ions, which are absent in distilled water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolytes** in water, such as salts, acids, and bases, dissociate into ions that facilitate the conduction of electricity.
 
• Pure water, such as distilled water, lacks these electrolytes, and thus, has very low conductivity.
 
• In practical applications, water conductivity is often used as an indicator of water purity.
 
• Water with high conductivity is generally considered less pure due to the presence of dissolved substances.

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is an autonomous agency of the Government of India, responsible for the management of a network of over 50,000 km of national highways.
 
• Established in 1988, NHAI's primary goal is to develop and maintain the national highways network to international standards.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and plays a crucial role in the economic development of the country by improving road connectivity.
 
• NHAI has been instrumental in implementing various flagship projects like the Golden Quadrilateral and the North-South and East-West Corridors.
